transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-09 15:00 PDT — Duration 42m — Attendees: Avery Chen, Diego Marquez (Redwood); Sofia Patel, Liam O'Connor, Priya Rao (NovaPay)

Summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on chat/text gen features: streaming responses, key request params (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences), and retry/idempotency patterns for reliable production usage. Customer is evaluating hosted first then potential Dedicated if latency/cost warrants.

Topics: Hosted API basics; streaming vs poll; param tuning for chat; retries, exponential backoff, idempotency; cost/latency tradeoffs; security/PII concerns.

[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Really excited to walk through the Hosted API chat/text basics, we'll show streaming, the SDK examples, and how to handle retries. Diego will jump into more of the technical bits.
[00:12] Sofia Patel: Hey, thanks. Quick context — we're building an in-app assistant for payments flows. Main constraints are p95 latency under 700ms for short prompts, and cost per transaction needs to be predictable. We're also sensitive to PII handling.
[00:25] Diego Marquez: Got it. We'll demo streaming because it helps with perceived latency and partial responses. Also show how to set temperature/top_p and deterministic options.
[00:40] Liam O'Connor: Curious how streaming integrates with our frontend. Any Socket vs SSE example?
[00:49] Diego Marquez: We have examples for WebSockets and Server-Sent Events in the SDK repo — I'll share the link. The basic flow: request with stream=true and you get chunked delta tokens; client assembles. We recommend small chunk sizes to update UI quickly.
[01:05] Priya Rao: How do you handle retries if a stream drops mid-response? We can't show partial/confusing outputs to end-users.
[01:12] Avery Chen: Good question. Two patterns: one is to use idempotency keys on requests plus a short window to resume from a cached prefix on the server — Redwood's hosted API supports prefix caching for the same conversation ID. Second is to implement client-side re-request with a 'resume' token; Diego will demo the SDK helper.
[01:30] Diego Marquez: Right, in practice we add a conversation_id and an idempotency_token header. If the connection drops, the client re-requests with the same token and the runtime can replay from last committed token. Demo snippet: // example pseudo-code shown in deck — note transcription may garble exact syntax. I'll paste repo link after the call.
[01:52] Sofia Patel: Sounds promising. On params — when should we tweak temperature vs top_p? Also how do you handle max_tokens in chat where we have system+history+user prompt?
[02:05] Diego Marquez: Temperature controls randomness; top_p is nucleus sampling. For deterministic answers, use low temp (0-0.2) and top_p 0.8-1. For creative copy, temp 0.7+. For max_tokens, Redwood returns token usage and we recommend calculating budget per request: reserved for response = model.max_sequence - prompt_tokens. For chat, we also suggest trimming or summarizing history using our built-in summarization shortcut to keep context within window.
[02:35] Liam O'Connor: What about cost visibility? We'll need token breakdown per route.
[02:40] Avery Chen: Console gives per-route and per-token cost breakdowns, plus a usage API. You can also tag requests server-side so purchases tie to product features; Diego: there's an example of per-route dashboards?
[02:50] Diego Marquez: Yep, in Console > Routes you can see token counts, latency buckets, and top error types. Very useful for tuning.
[03:03] Priya Rao: Security — we need SOC 2 plus audit logs, KMS, and optional VPC peering. Does hosted support that?
[03:10] Avery Chen: Our hosted API supports customer-managed KMS for encrypting keys at rest and we have SOC 2 Type II. For strict network isolation we offer Private deployments, but many customers use hosted with VPC Peering + strict retention controls. We'll share our security pack.
[03:28] Sofia Patel: Great. Back to streaming: are there implications for token billing? If a partial stream is sent then aborted, are tokens billed?
[03:36] Diego Marquez: Billing is based on tokens generated/committed by the inference runtime. If a response is cut early and wasn't committed, typically fewer tokens billed. But if you resume and re-generate overlapping tokens, those count — which is why we advise using prefix caching and idempotency to avoid double-generation.
[03:56] Liam O'Connor: What about throttling and rate limits for bursts? We expect bursts around payroll runs.
[04:03] Avery Chen: Hosted tiers have rate limits and burst allowances. For bursty production patterns we recommend Dedicated capacity or configuring burst capacity add-ons. Also Adaptive batching in the runtime helps overall throughput.
[04:18] Diego Marquez: I'll call out an implementation detail: continuous batching groups small requests into GPU batches while trying to respect latency SLOs. That helps lower per-token cost without adding tail latency.
[04:34] Sofia Patel: Can we see the SDK example for streaming and retry logic now?
[04:38] Diego Marquez: Sure, sharing my screen — pulling up the SDK example: Node snippet with eventsource and exponential backoff. Example pseudo: const stream = client.chat.stream({model: 'redwood-xx', conversation_id, stream: true, temperature: 0.2}); stream.on('delta', chunk => updateUI(chunk)); stream.on('error', err => handleRetry(err));
[05:00] (screen share glitches briefly)
[05:08] Speaker 1: Sorry, slight lag — network blip.
[05:12] Diego Marquez: Back — as a best practice, on error we do exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 attempts for idempotent reads. For non-idempotent ops (like creating a new resource), require server-side dedupe.
[05:30] Priya Rao: For banking transcripts we must ensure PII is not kept. How does retention work?
[05:38] Avery Chen: Hosted has configurable retention windows per account, plus opt-in to not retain full prompt/response for certain routes. For regulated customers we recommend Private or Dedicated with on-prem options. We'll attach retention options doc.
[05:52] Sofia Patel: Any concerns about hallucinations for factual prompts? We need reliability for confirmation messages like payment amounts and beneficiary names.
[05:59] Diego Marquez: For high-accuracy tasks we suggest chain-of-thought suppression, lower temperature, and using verification steps: e.g., system prompt instructs to respond only with data from the payload and return 'UNKNOWN' if not present. Also consider reranking with a higher-precision model or run a deterministic check using embeddings/nearest-neighbor.
[06:25] Liam O'Connor: Can you do on-the-fly model swapping — host a cheaper fast model and fallback to a qc model if confidence low?
[06:33] Avery Chen: Yes, Smart routing supports policy-based routing — you can set rules by latency, cost, or confidence score that route to different model variants and automatically fallback. That's part of Redwood's runtime.
[06:45] Priya Rao: How do you surface confidence? Is it log-likelihood or something else?
[06:50] Diego Marquez: We expose token logprobs and a built-in confidence heuristic; you can also plug in custom evals. Console surfaces low-confidence alerts and regression detection over your prompt sets.
[07:05] Sofia Patel: Ok, let's talk about retries in more detail — if we re-request a response we could end up charging twice. How does Redwood prevent double billing?
[07:13] Diego Marquez: Two mechanisms: idempotency tokens to dedupe generation server-side, and cached prefixes. It doesn't fully eliminate re-generation charges if the model needs to recompute, but it minimizes redundant work by replaying cached KV state. We'll demo a retry flow in the SDK.
[07:33] (brief side conversation about integration timeline)
[07:40] Liam O'Connor: What are typical tradeoffs when switching to Dedicated later?
[07:44] Avery Chen: Dedicated gives you guaranteed capacity, lower p95 latency, and predictable cost for high throughput. Tradeoffs: you'd manage more deployment config but Redwood handles orchestration. Many customers start hosted to validate and move to Dedicated as they scale.
[07:58] Priya Rao: If we go hosted initially, can we ensure data residency in EU?
[08:03] Avery Chen: Yes, you can pin region and we have EU regions for data residency. For stricter legal requirements Private is recommended but hosted regional pinning satisfies most customers.
[08:15] Sofia Patel: Any integration examples for server-side batching? We have a microservice that aggregates prompts; would Redwood batch across customers?
[08:22] Diego Marquez: Batching happens in the runtime across requests to the same model; multi-tenant batching is safe and isolated. You can also use client-side batching to aggregate low-priority prompts.
[08:35] (Diego posts links in chat: https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-api, https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-examples)
[08:45] Liam O'Connor: We'll need SSO and RBAC — admin console access for ops, dev keys for engineering.
[08:51] Avery Chen: Supported. Console has RBAC with role templates and SSO via SAML or OIDC. We'll send the security matrix.
[09:00] Priya Rao: For the pilot, we want to test 500 RPS with median latencies under 500ms for our smallest prompts. Can hosted meet that?
[09:07] Diego Marquez: Depends on model choice and token lengths. For short prompts on optimized models, hosted can hit those numbers at modest cost; if sustained 500 RPS, Dedicated might be more cost-effective. We recommend a short benchmark: you provide the prompt set and target concurrency, we run a spike test and share numbers.
[09:25] Avery Chen: We'll draft a pilot plan: goals, success criteria (p95 < 700ms, cost less than $X per txn), timeline.
[09:33] Sofia Patel: Nice. Any final clarifications on streaming and retries?
[09:38] Diego Marquez: Quick recap: use stream=true for user-facing perceived latency; include conversation_id and idempotency_token headers; use exponential backoff with jitter on errors; leverage prefix caching and conversation summaries to reduce re-generation; and monitor token billing in Console.
[09:55] (short silence)
[10:00] Avery Chen: Alright — recap of next steps: I'll send pricing + SOW; Diego will share SDK examples and streaming repo; NovaPay provide prompt set and concurrency targets; schedule pilot kickoff next week. We'll attach security docs.
[10:14] Priya Rao: Sounds good — thanks everyone.
[10:16] Sofia Patel: Thanks — excited to try the streaming SDK.
[10:18] Meeting end.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional speaker mis-attribution and minor transcription errors as typical for automated meeting exports. Links mentioned in chat: https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-api, https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-examples, security pack link will be emailed.
